name: Cognition of Figural Units
description: Ability to visually identify and recognize whole objects, figures, or geometric forms even when partially obscured, incomplete, or presented in unfamiliar orientations.
educationalSignificance: Fundamental for quick visual perception, sight-word recognition, reading speed, diagram interpretation, and spatial orientation.

interpretationRules.strength: Exceptional visual closure skills; rapidly perceives visual wholes and decodes complex graphic material with minimal effort.
interpretationRules.priority: Difficulty with visual closure may lead to hesitations when interpreting partial diagrams, cluttered worksheets, or unfamiliar font typography.

name: Cognition of Figural Classes
description: Ability to group, categorize, and discover sorting rules for visual objects and geometric figures based on abstract physical properties (shape, orientation, symmetry, texture).
educationalSignificance: Underpins early scientific classification, geometric intuition, visual organization, and the ability to find common features among visual concepts.

interpretationRules.strength: Quickly discovers underlying structural visual patterns and creates logical groupings of abstract visual stimuli.
interpretationRules.priority: May struggle to notice subtle categorizing rules in visual data; benefits from explicit visual attribute checklists.

name: Cognition of Figural Relations
description: Ability to understand the spatial rule or geometric transformation connecting one figure to another and apply that identical relationship to a novel target (A : B :: C : D).
educationalSignificance: Critical for higher-order spatial reasoning, geometry, architectural comprehension, visual problem-solving, and STEM modeling.

interpretationRules.strength: Superior ability to deduce geometric transformations (rotations, reflections, topological changes) and extrapolate spatial rules.
interpretationRules.priority: Visual analogical reasoning requires systematic step-by-step feature breakdown and guided transformation training.

name: Memory for Figural Units
description: Ability to retain and accurately recall specific visual figures, symbols, patterns, or spatial layouts after a brief exposure delay.
educationalSignificance: Vital for retaining board notes, copying from distance, spelling retention through visual imagery, and remembering map features.

interpretationRules.strength: High-capacity visual memory buffer; effortlessly preserves precise geometric arrangements and visual details.
interpretationRules.priority: Tends to lose visual detail over short delays; benefits from multimodal encoding (labeling visuals with words).

name: Evaluation of Figural Units
description: Ability to critically compare multiple visual objects and make rapid, exact judgments about identity, minute discrepancy, or geometric flaws.
educationalSignificance: Essential for proofreading, catching editing errors in written work, technical drawing accuracy, and fine visual motor precision.

interpretationRules.strength: Acute visual error detection and discernment; rapidly spots minor anomalies and precision inconsistencies.
interpretationRules.priority: May overlook fine details or jump to conclusions without systematic scanning of visual boundaries.

name: Evaluation of Figural Classes
description: Ability to evaluate a collection of visual items, verify whether they satisfy a common rule, and accurately reject items that do not belong.
educationalSignificance: Supports analytical sorting, quality control in design and technical tasks, and validation of visual solutions.

interpretationRules.strength: Quickly validates class boundaries and spots subtle inconsistencies across complex visual sets.
interpretationRules.priority: Requires targeted practice verifying each item's characteristics against explicit criteria before judging.

name: Convergent Production of Figural Units
description: Ability to synthesize individual visual pieces, components, or geometric shapes into a unified, correct target structure (tangram-style synthesis).
educationalSignificance: Crucial for engineering design, physical modeling, map assembly, puzzle solving, and mechanical comprehension.

interpretationRules.strength: Outstanding spatial synthesis and mental rotation; easily arranges parts into coherent functional wholes.
interpretationRules.priority: Needs scaffolded visual assembly tasks starting from 2-piece composites to multi-element configurations.

name: Cognition of Symbolic Systems
description: Ability to discover underlying organizational principles, mathematical progressions, numeric intervals, and alphanumeric rule systems.
educationalSignificance: Core foundation for algebra, number sense, algorithmic reasoning, computer programming, and formula comprehension.

interpretationRules.strength: Rapidly extracts mathematical rules and sequential logic from numeric or code-based sequences.
interpretationRules.priority: Benefits from concrete number-line representations and verbalization of step-by-step arithmetic transitions.

name: Memory for Symbolic Units
description: Ability to accurately retain and recall arbitrary letters, numbers, digits, symbols, or phone/ID codes over short-term holding intervals.
educationalSignificance: Critical for mental math, following multi-digit arithmetic steps, remembering passwords, formulas, and spelling sequences.

interpretationRules.strength: High symbolic working-memory span; comfortably manipulates multi-digit numeric items without dropping characters.
interpretationRules.priority: Vulnerable to symbolic cognitive overload; benefits from chunking techniques and written scratchpads.

name: Memory for Symbolic Units (Auditory)
description: Ability to encode, hold, and reproduce spoken sequences of numbers, letters, or phonemes presented strictly in the auditory channel.
educationalSignificance: Essential for following spoken classroom directions, retaining oral phone numbers, and phonological processing during language acquisition.

interpretationRules.strength: Strong auditory-verbal memory loop; effortlessly repeats complex oral instructions and multi-part data.
interpretationRules.priority: Easily drops oral instructions; requires visual reinforcement and sub-vocal rehearsal strategies.

name: Convergent Production of Symbolic Transformations
description: Ability to manipulate, rearrange, and transform symbolic equations, code strings, or mathematical representations to achieve a specified target output.
educationalSignificance: Drives algebraic manipulation, coding logic, equation solving, cipher decoding, and chemical formula balancing.

interpretationRules.strength: Nimble symbolic flexibility; effortlessly solves algebraic unknowns and transforms expressions.
interpretationRules.priority: May become rigid in applying initial formulas; needs explicit training in reverse operations and algebraic factoring.

name: Cognition of Semantic Units (Reading)
description: Ability to accurately grasp the precise meaning of words, concepts, idiomatic terms, and contextual nuances in written language.
educationalSignificance: The primary predictor of reading comprehension, textbook learning, academic vocabulary mastery, and essay writing.

interpretationRules.strength: Rich vocabulary knowledge and acute contextual deduction when encountering complex text.
interpretationRules.priority: Benefits from explicit morphology instruction, root word analysis, and semantic mapping.

name: Cognition of Semantic Relations
description: Ability to discern the conceptual relationship connecting two words or ideas and apply that exact relationship to another semantic pair (e.g., Cause : Effect, Part : Whole).
educationalSignificance: Core component of verbal IQ, standardized admissions tests, critical reading, scientific reasoning, and essay argumentation.

interpretationRules.strength: High verbal reasoning facility; quickly grasps hierarchical, functional, and causal analogies.
interpretationRules.priority: Needs structured relationship taxonomy practice (synonym, antonym, degree, part-whole, cause-effect).

name: Cognition of Semantic Systems
description: Ability to comprehend interconnected structures of ideas, argumentative threads, sequential narratives, and inferential logic in multi-sentence passages.
educationalSignificance: Critical for reading complex literature, understanding historical narratives, following extended scientific explanations, and academic synthesis.

interpretationRules.strength: Superb deep comprehension and synthesis across complex thematic passages.
interpretationRules.priority: Tends to fixate on isolated sentences; benefits from paragraph structure mapping and main-idea extraction protocols.

name: Cognition of Figural Systems
description: Ability to understand complex 2D and 3D geometric grids, coordinate layouts, isometric projections, and spatial matrix systems.
educationalSignificance: High value for mechanical drafting, trigonometry, physics vector spaces, and advanced 3D modeling.

interpretationRules.strength: Easily navigates complex multi-dimensional spatial representations.
interpretationRules.priority: Needs practice with grid coordinate transformations and folded cube projections.

name: Cognition of Figural Transformations
description: Ability to mentally rotate, fold, unfold, or invert complex 2D surfaces and 3D solids to predict their altered appearance.
educationalSignificance: Essential for dental/surgical spatial skills, organic chemistry stereochemistry, engineering CAD design.

interpretationRules.strength: Swift, accurate mental rotation and surface-folding visualization.
interpretationRules.priority: Requires physical paper folding and interactive 3D rotation manipulation exercises.

name: Memory for Figural Systems
description: Ability to retain and reproduce the exact spatial coordinates, routes, or relative positions of multiple objects across a map or board.
educationalSignificance: Vital for geography, tactical navigation, lab layout retention, and sports play execution.

interpretationRules.strength: Exceptional photographic spatial memory for map layouts and positions.
interpretationRules.priority: Benefits from landmark-anchoring and grid-cell mental tagging.

name: Divergent Production of Figural Units
description: Ability to rapidly generate numerous distinct, original visual designs, shapes, or functional interpretations starting from simple geometric prompts.
educationalSignificance: Key driver of artistic creativity, architectural ideation, UI/UX concept sketching, and industrial design.

interpretationRules.strength: Prolific visual brainstorming; produces diverse, unconventional graphical concepts.
interpretationRules.priority: Benefits from morphological matrix brainstorming and visual attribute modification drills.

name: Cognition of Symbolic Relations
description: Ability to deduce relational rules connecting alphanumeric or mathematical terms and project those relations onto corresponding symbolic pairs.
educationalSignificance: Essential for mastering algebraic ratios, unit conversions, physics ratios, and formal logic syntax.

interpretationRules.strength: Precise mathematical ratio intuition and symbolic correspondence discovery.
interpretationRules.priority: Requires step-by-step fractional and relational reduction modeling.

name: Memory for Symbolic Systems
description: Ability to retain and reproduce structured symbolic sequences (like math proofs, coding routines, or musical sheet patterns).
educationalSignificance: Supports multi-step mental calculus, code debugging without reference docs, and musical sight-reading.

interpretationRules.strength: High-capacity symbolic string memory buffer.
interpretationRules.priority: Benefits from hierarchical mnemonic tagging and rhythm-based grouping.

name: Evaluation of Symbolic Systems
description: Ability to audit mathematical operations, balance checks, or code structures to spot logical inconsistencies or computation syntax errors.
educationalSignificance: Crucial for mathematical error-checking, accounting audits, software code testing, and logic verification.

interpretationRules.strength: Rigorous symbolic proof-checking and computational flaw detection.
interpretationRules.priority: Needs structured line-by-line verification protocols and assertion testing habits.

name: Divergent Production of Symbolic Relations
description: Ability to generate multiple different valid mathematical equations, algebraic pathways, or algorithmic solutions for a single numerical goal.
educationalSignificance: Fosters flexible mathematical thinking, algorithmic optimization, and creative quantitative problem solving.

interpretationRules.strength: Remarkable numeric agility; discovers non-standard mathematical paths to reach targets.
interpretationRules.priority: Benefits from Target-Number challenges (e.g. 24 Game) and equation diversification drills.

name: Cognition of Semantic Classes
description: Ability to categorize abstract verbal ideas, scientific concepts, or thematic arguments into overarching taxonomic categories.
educationalSignificance: Underpins essay structuring, scientific taxonomy, social science classifications, and philosophical analysis.

interpretationRules.strength: Quickly organizes complex verbal knowledge into robust hierarchical categories.
interpretationRules.priority: Benefits from concept webbing, semantic Venn diagrams, and taxonomic outlines.

name: Cognition of Semantic Transformations
description: Ability to interpret metaphorical shifts, idioms, puns, double meanings, and conceptual reinterpretations in language.
educationalSignificance: Essential for literary analysis, understanding irony/satire, high-level negotiation, and rhetorical analysis.

interpretationRules.strength: Effortlessly navigates nuanced figurative language, irony, and layered metaphors.
interpretationRules.priority: May interpret idioms too literally; benefits from explicit figurative idiom breakdowns.

name: Cognition of Semantic Implications
description: Ability to foresee subsequent consequences, unstated intentions, and logical ramifications emerging from a scenario or argument.
educationalSignificance: Key for critical reading, anticipating counterarguments, scientific hypothesis prediction, and strategic decision making.

interpretationRules.strength: Sharp deductive foresight; accurately projects future implications of complex situations.
interpretationRules.priority: Needs explicit 'What If?' causal chain worksheets and hypothesis-testing frameworks.

name: Memory for Semantic Units
description: Ability to retain and recall meaningful verbal facts, definitions, names, and biographical information over delayed intervals.
educationalSignificance: Critical for history, biology, law, medicine, and fact-heavy academic disciplines.

interpretationRules.strength: High-retention verbal fact reservoir; readily retrieves declarative knowledge.
interpretationRules.priority: Benefits from spaced retrieval practice and semantic association networks.

name: Evaluation of Semantic Systems
description: Ability to critically evaluate an extended argumentative essay, detect logical fallacies, assess evidentiary credibility, and evaluate internal coherence.
educationalSignificance: The ultimate skill in critical thinking, scientific peer review, debate, media literacy, and academic research.

interpretationRules.strength: Rigorous critical reasoning; immediately pinpoints logical fallacies and weak premises.
interpretationRules.priority: Needs structured Toulmin argument modeling and fallacy identification practice.

name: Convergent Production of Semantic Systems
description: Ability to synthesize disparate factual points, evidence, and premises into a unified, logically organized narrative or explanatory essay.
educationalSignificance: Crucial for research report writing, synthesizing complex technical documentation, and coherent presentation.

interpretationRules.strength: Outstanding synthesis capacity; unites fragmented data points into cohesive logical structures.
interpretationRules.priority: Requires structured outlining protocols and paragraph transition scaffolding.

name: Divergent Production of Semantic Units
description: Ability to rapidly generate a large number of diverse, imaginative ideas, word associations, or creative titles under open-ended criteria.
educationalSignificance: Drives creative writing, advertising copywriting, innovative business brainstorming, and lateral thinking.

interpretationRules.strength: Prolific verbal creativity; excels in unconstrained idea generation and creative writing.
interpretationRules.priority: Benefits from SCAMPER ideation prompts and lateral thinking drills.

name: Divergent Production of Semantic Relations
description: Ability to bridge two completely unrelated domains by inventing novel analogies, poetic metaphors, or innovative cross-disciplinary connections.
educationalSignificance: Underlies visionary scientific breakthroughs, evocative literary poetry, and cross-disciplinary innovation.

interpretationRules.strength: Visionary cross-domain synthesizer; generates profound metaphors and novel conceptual bridges.
interpretationRules.priority: Needs guided exercises linking disparate sciences/humanities concepts.
